### Claim 1 — R1 per-call retain in `retain_pinned_calls_on_node`
**Verdict:** PASS
**Evidence:** `src/types/context.rs:755-832`. The pinned branch resolves the cluster's call node and invokes the helper (`:727-729`). Inside `retain_pinned_calls_on_node`:
- It builds `call_ids` over EVERY `Content::ToolCall` in content order via `.iter().enumerate().filter_map(...)` (`:767-783`) — NOT first-only (this is the fix for #77 F-3 "first-call-only").
- Per call (`for call_id in &call_ids`, `:791`): if a result is live on-trunk → `continue` (keep, atomic) `:792-800`; else if a result is a DIRECT child (`lm.parent_id == Some(this_node_id)` AND `tool_call_id == call_id`) → push to `results_to_append` (re-append from forensic `self.messages`) `:802-813`; else → push to `ids_to_drop` `:814`.
- Drops are applied with sibling-preserving `content.retain(|b| !matches!(... if ids_to_drop.contains(id)))` `:818-826` — only the abandoned call is removed, live siblings stay. Re-appends are inserted right after the call node preserving order `:829-831`. Abandoned work is never re-materialised (no path appends a non-direct-child result); no dangling call (every dropped call is removed from content). Test `row_pinned_revert_to_first_result_now_call_atomic` (`:3237`) and `row_pinned_revert_to_call_node_now_call_atomic` (`:3261`) exercise the drop-and-re-append behaviours, asserting `!trunk_has_dangling_call` + `pcall_a` kept + `pcall_b` not re-materialised.
